assumptions: The product remains a software and records layer: registered processors and other qualified operators retain title or custody where applicable, feed-safety decisions, classification, sampling, transport, processing, recall execution, and statutory liability.

The founder can use a qualified feed-law or veterinary adviser and keep the initial build, enterprise sale, and bounded onboarding within 25 hours per week without using confidential employer information.
The proposed 500-1500 PLN monthly price per active stream, 65-80% contribution margin, 300-stream scale, renewal, and valuation path are planning hypotheses rather than established outcomes.
The final-version processor-led structure is assessed using the supplied bound research; no unreported processor commitment, generator adoption, data right, or market-size evidence is assumed.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed paid pilot with a registered independent processor that mandates use by at least three recurring generator streams, grants lawful continuing record rights, records actual sales and onboarding cost, and demonstrates conversion or renewal at a price supported by measured labor, rejection, audit, or recall savings and a defensible contribution margin.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The redesign correctly moves the control point from one-off matching to the processor's recurring, mandatory intake and traceability workflow. That aligns the product with genuine feed-hygiene, qualification, exception, and recall obligations and turns one processor into both buyer and supplier-onboarding channel. The insight is only moderately distinctive because the supplied evidence shows integrated processors already combining registration, weighing, compliance support, logistics, and processing; it does not establish an unserved independent software layer.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Stream qualification, traceability, contamination control, acceptance records, and recall readiness are important recurring responsibilities, so there is a credible operational pain basis. However, the evidence does not show that independent processors consider their existing workflow inadequate, will mandate a third-party product, or will pay 500-1500 PLN per stream each month. Because incumbents bundle these functions with physical operations, the standalone budget and urgency remain uncertain rather than demonstrated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A processor-paid software licence can in principle be asset-light and high-margin if all laboratories, transport, storage, processing, safety, and product-liability work stays with qualified counterparties. The proposed contribution margin, price, 300 active streams, 25% EBITDA, five-to-seven-year scale path, CAC, payback, churn, and six-times valuation are unvalidated sensitivities. Enterprise selling, stream-specific configuration, supplier onboarding, support, and legal or insurance work could make delivery service-heavy, while processor concentration makes LTV and cash generation fragile.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Independent registered Polish feed processors onboarding recurring plant-only former-food streams form a coherent, narrow beachhead, and the official register makes the buyer universe identifiable. Industrial activity confirms that former-food feed is real. The supplied research does not quantify eligible processors, uncontracted streams, viable tonnage or radius, or the subset lacking adequate incumbent systems, so the economically accessible software beachhead may be much smaller than the underlying material flow.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A processor mandate could create a strong position inside one customer's supplier network, but the processor owns that relationship and can build, bundle, replace, or discontinue the software. IUNGO already operates in Poland, Trotec is adding Polish capacity, and Trotec and FeedValid bundle operational infrastructure, data, registration, logistics, and compliance. No exclusive input source, privileged distribution agreement, or sharply underserved processor segment supports a credible domination path yet.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: If one workflow becomes trusted, the same records architecture could extend to more generators, processors, eligible streams, quality forecasting, exception analytics, recall modules, and nearby EU markets. An anchor can also provide a useful product template. Expansion is constrained by processor-specific integrations, local legal interpretation, stream-level rules, and the need to win a new controlling relationship in each processor network, so the first win does not automatically unlock adjacent revenue.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Longitudinal specifications, tests, acceptances, volumes, and rejection reasons could create switching costs and better qualification logic. That advantage exists only if processors contractually mandate the workflow, grant continuing lawful record rights, contribute sufficient repeated data, and do not reserve the same data for themselves. The customer can refuse or revoke those rights, incumbents already capture operational data, and no network effect, exclusive data source, certification, or difficult technical capability is established.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A focused processor-branded product could be faster to deploy than custom internal software, remove two-sided marketplace friction, and give smaller processors structured records without taking physical risk. The packet supplies no measured reduction in labor, rejection loss, recall exposure, onboarding time, or audit cost, and no capability that integrated processors or ordinary workflow vendors clearly cannot reproduce. The advantage is plausible convenience, not yet a behavior-changing or economically decisive improvement.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: EU support for safely redirecting eligible former food into feed, established feed rules, visible Polish processing activity, and a new Trotec facility show sector momentum and recurring compliance needs. The same evidence also shows a maturing operational market with capable incumbents. The regulatory duties are not a newly created software opening, and prevention or human redistribution remains prior where food is still suitable, so timing is supportive but not uniquely favorable.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Selling to a finite public list of registered processors and letting one anchor invite three to five contracted generators is materially more credible than acquiring both sides of an open exchange. It gives a bounded first-customer route and can make generator participation part of an existing commercial relationship. The anchor sale is nevertheless trust-heavy, likely consultative, and wholly unvalidated; processors may reject an independent system or data terms, and acquisition cost, cycle length, pilot conversion, and repeatability across processors are unknown.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The data, workflow, and exception product fits the founder's technical strengths, a bounded pilot is compatible with the stated capital and time limits, and AI can accelerate normal product and analytics work. Execution remains conditional on expert feed-law guidance, accepted liability allocation, insurance, secure integrations, reliable generator records, and strict retention of safety and emergency duties by qualified operators. These requirements appear obtainable but cannot be replaced by software or part-time founder effort, and the platform's own regulatory status remains unresolved.

highest_value_structural_change: Make the product a contractually embedded white-label intake module for a committed independent processor, priced as a multi-year site licence against verified operating savings rather than an assumed per-stream fee, while securing anonymized cross-processor benchmarking rights that survive individual supplier relationships; without those rights, remove the data-moat claim and compete explicitly as a focused workflow vendor.
main_structural_strength: The processor-led design collapses a two-sided marketplace into one accountable buyer and embeds supplier onboarding in recurring offtake relationships, creating a plausible route to repeated use without taking physical custody or feed-safety responsibility.
primary_score_limiter: There is no direct evidence that an independent processor will simultaneously pay the proposed price, mandate supplier use, renew the product, and grant durable record rights; those four conditions underpin revenue, distribution, retention, and the proposed data moat.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: IUNGO already sources and processes food-sector streams in Poland, while Trotec and FeedValid bundle containers, transport, weighing, registration, processing, data, and compliance support, indicating that the relevant workflow is commonly integrated with physical operations rather than purchased as a standalone software layer.
